about: Held-out material that no model has read (or has read only in part) is not shipped, so it can still serve as held-out material. Each file's SHA-256 equals the one in its study's FROZEN.md, so it can be checked when it is released. The paper's number scripts read the counts they quote from here.

D3-indentation/data/r2gen/part-held.json.why_not_shipped: D3 round-2 reserve: 4,000 generated programs (seeds 200000-203999), sealed 8 Nov 2026 and never read by a model or script for results (PROTOCOL-2.md: 'not used and stays sealed as a reserve')

D4-ordinal-suffixes/data/part-reserve.js.why_not_shipped: D4 round-1 reserve part (items in round-1 reserve frames), sealed 7 Nov 2026 and never read as a file; X1's ordinal material later used its frames and half of its numbers (X1-shared-parts/data/ord/)

D4-ordinal-suffixes/data2/frames2.jsonl.why_not_shipped: D4 round-2 held-out frames: holds the 5 date frames that no model has read (the tests used the 19 ranking, position and anniversary frames, whose items are in the round-2 confirmation outputs); the frozen loader checks the whole file's digest, so it cannot be shipped without them

D5-capitals/data/headings-reserve.jsonl.why_not_shipped: D5 round-2 held-out heading items: items 0-499 (after the loader's seed-0 shuffle) were read by the round-2 confirmation; the other 835 of 1,335 were never read
